article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Afghani × Hawaiian × Skunk #1
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: 1.1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Forest fruits, pineapple, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: First to second week of October
Indoor Yield: 550–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 2 kg per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Morning Glory is a reminder that fruit-forward cannabis existed long before modern breeding became dominated by candy, dessert, and Gelato-derived genetics. Barney’s Farm built this award-winning cultivar from Afghani, Hawaiian, and Skunk #1, creating weed that combines tropical fruit and citrus with the earthy pungency of older Afghan and Skunk lines. The finished hybrid sits at approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica, yet its personality is more balanced than those numbers suggest. Cerebral energy and sociability arrive early, while the Afghan influence supplies enough physical ease to keep the high from becoming excessively sharp.

In the garden, the cultivar is equally practical: indoor plants stay around one meter tall, require only a short vegetative period, and can finish flowering in roughly 60–65 days. Barney’s Farm currently lists THC at 20% and indoor production around 550–650 g/m², while exceptionally large greenhouse or outdoor plants can exceed two kilograms under ideal conditions. Morning Glory also earned first place overall at the 2002 High Times Cannabis Cup , establishing its reputation during one of the most competitive periods in Amsterdam cannabis culture.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed lineage is Afghani × Hawaiian × Skunk #1. Barney’s Farm describes the cultivar as a three-way cross designed to combine the Kush-like physical character of Afghani cannabis with Hawaiian citrus influence and the cerebral qualities of Skunk #1. The completed plant is classified as 60% sativa and 40% indica, an unusual balance considering the strong physical traits contributed by the Afghan side. Hawaiian genetics push the strain toward brighter aromas and greater mental energy, while Skunk #1 adds vigor, hybrid strength, resin production, and the unmistakable pungency associated with one of modern marijuana breeding’s most influential families.

Each genetic component remains recognizable in the finished cultivar. Afghani ancestry contributes sturdier structure, substantial resin, and a relaxing foundation beneath the high. Hawaiian influence provides fruit, pineapple, floral tones, and a more expansive character. Skunk #1 links those qualities together with vigorous growth and an animated cerebral effect. Rather than allowing one side of the pedigree to dominate completely, Barney’s Farm selected Morning Glory to retain attributes from all three. That balanced breeding also helps explain its competition success: the plant delivers sativa-style energy without requiring the extreme height or lengthy maturation associated with many traditional tropical varieties.
Effects and Experience

Morning Glory usually begins with a noticeable cerebral rise. Mood can brighten quickly, conversation becomes easier, and ordinary activities may acquire a more engaging quality. Barney’s Farm describes the effects as talkative, social, creative, and energizing, which makes the cultivar especially well suited to recreational situations where interaction matters. Music, casual creative work, outdoor activities, gaming, or time with friends can pair naturally with moderate amounts. The mental stimulation is substantial but generally less aggressive than an uncompromising Haze, in part because the Afghan component gives the experience a physical anchor.

That body component develops more clearly as time passes. Muscular tension may soften and the pace can become calmer without immediately turning into couch-lock. In smaller amounts, Morning Glory can remain functional and animated for much of the experience; heavier consumption is more likely to reveal the indica side, producing greater physical relaxation, distraction, and eventual sluggishness. At approximately 20% THC according to the current breeder specification, the strain is potent enough that inexperienced consumers should still begin conservatively. The combination of mental lift and gradual body relaxation is a central reason Morning Glory has remained memorable rather than simply becoming another early-2000s sativa hybrid.
Medical Benefits

Medical cannabis consumers may be drawn to Morning Glory when they want an uplifting cultivar that does not immediately produce heavy sedation. Marijuana with this type of profile is sometimes preferred during periods of everyday stress, reduced motivation, or low appetite because the first stage can remain active and socially comfortable. The later physical component may offer temporary relaxation when muscular tension or minor discomfort accompanies mental stress.

Morning Glory itself has not been demonstrated through controlled clinical trials to treat depression, anxiety, chronic pain, fatigue, or another specific condition. A strain name also cannot guarantee an identical cannabinoid or terpene profile from every harvest. THC-rich cannabis may increase anxiety, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, or impaired coordination in sensitive consumers, particularly when the dose is high. Anyone using weed medicinally should therefore place greater weight on laboratory results from the specific product and qualified medical guidance than on general strain reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The flavor is one of Morning Glory’s strongest distinguishing features. Barney’s Farm lists forest fruits, pineapple, floral notes, and a mild finish among its primary taste characteristics. The aroma moves in a darker direction, combining spice, pungency, earth, and Skunk. Those contrasting layers allow the strain to smell much more traditional than its tropical flavor might initially suggest. Opening a cured flower can reveal ripe fruit and citrus first, followed by damp earth, herbs, pepper, and unmistakable old-school cannabis funk.

Pineapple becomes particularly noticeable when the flower is smoked or vaporized, while forest-berry sweetness can remain through the middle of the inhale. Peppery spice and Skunk tend to linger on the finish. Barney’s historical strain guide also emphasized intense pine and forest-fruit characteristics. No universal terpene analysis is published by the breeder, so presenting one rigid terpene hierarchy would be misleading. Limonene is consistent with the citrus side, caryophyllene with pepper and spice, and myrcene with earthy fruit qualities, but the dominant compounds can shift according to phenotype, environment, harvest timing, and curing.
Growing Information

Morning Glory was bred to provide strong sativa qualities without creating an unnecessarily difficult indoor plant. Barney’s Farm says the cultivar is vigorous enough that approximately two weeks of vegetative growth can be sufficient before flowering begins. Indoor plants normally reach about 100 cm and require roughly 60–65 days in bloom. Under favorable conditions, the breeder reports approximately 550–650 g/m². This compact size makes the plant easier to accommodate than tall tropical sativas, while enough branching remains to support multiple productive flower sites.

The buds develop into thick, resinous colas rather than extremely loose Haze-style flowers. Growers can use low-stress training or a level canopy to distribute light across the branching structure, although prolonged vegetative growth is generally unnecessary. Strong airflow becomes useful as the flowers gain density, particularly in the later weeks. The cultivar’s resin production also makes the flowers and trim potentially attractive for concentrate or hash production . Aroma control should not be overlooked; spicy Skunk and pungent earth become considerably stronger once flowering is established.

Outdoor and greenhouse cultivation can produce much larger plants. Barney’s Farm states that exceptional specimens may exceed two kilograms per plant under ideal conditions, with harvest occurring during the first or second week of October. That figure represents high-end breeder potential rather than an ordinary expected yield. Reaching anything close to it requires substantial root space, strong sunlight, a long vegetative season, good nutrition, and favorable weather. Nevertheless, the cultivar’s combination of relatively early October maturity and large production potential makes it practical in more temperate climates than many sativa-dominant marijuana strains .
FAQ
What are the genetics of Morning Glory?

Morning Glory from Barney’s Farm is a three-way cross of Afghani, Hawaiian, and Skunk #1. The breeder designed the hybrid to combine Afghan physical character, Hawaiian citrus and tropical influence, and the cerebral high associated with Skunk #1.
Is Morning Glory indica or sativa?

Morning Glory is approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its effects generally begin energetic, creative, and social before the indica component produces greater physical relaxation later in the experience.
How much THC does Morning Glory have?

Barney’s Farm currently lists Morning Glory at approximately 20% THC. Actual potency can vary according to phenotype, cultivation conditions, plant health, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology.
What does Morning Glory taste like?

Forest fruits, pineapple, citrus, and mild floral sweetness form the fruitier side of the profile, while spice, earth, pepper, and Skunk provide a more pungent background. Barney’s Farm specifically lists forest fruits, pineapple, floral flavors, and a spicy, earthy, Skunky aroma.
Did Morning Glory win a Cannabis Cup?

Yes. Morning Glory from Barney’s won first place overall at the 2002 High Times Cannabis Cup in Amsterdam. The award helped establish the cultivar as one of Barney’s Farm’s important early competition strains.
Final Thoughts on Morning Glory

Morning Glory combines three foundational cannabis traditions without losing the identity of any of them. Afghani genetics provide structure and a physical foundation, Hawaiian influence adds tropical fruit and citrus, and Skunk #1 supplies vigor, pungency, and cerebral energy. The resulting weed feels lively and social at first but becomes increasingly relaxed as the experience develops, making it more balanced than a conventional high-energy sativa.

Its garden performance strengthens the appeal. Approximately two weeks of vegetative growth can be enough, flowering takes only 60–65 days, indoor plants stay around one meter tall, and optimized yields can reach 550–650 g/m². Outdoors or in a greenhouse, Barney’s Farm reports exceptional potential above two kilograms per plant, with harvest arriving during early October.

The cultivar’s 2002 Cannabis Cup victory gives it genuine historical weight, but Morning Glory does not need the award to remain interesting. Tropical fruit, pineapple, earthy Skunk, substantial resin, manageable growth, and a distinctive transition from energetic cerebral effects toward physical calm give this Barney’s Farm hybrid an identity that still holds up decades after its introduction.
